Article Title: Inspiring story on fatherhood: "I love my girls. They teach me things sometimes when I think that I’m trying to teach them" - How Jason Kelce’s four daughters changed his life beyond football
Article Text:
How Jason Kelce found a different kind of success through fatherhood

Why Jason and Kylie Kelce use a divide-and-conquer approach

How Kylie Kelce is teaching her daughters confidence and body positivity

What Jason and Kylie Kelce want their children to learn about life

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce spent his NFL career absorbing lessons from coaches, teammates and opponents. But according to the former Philadelphia Eagles center, some of his most meaningful lessons have come from his daughters. Fatherhood has changed the way he sees success, patience and family, giving the retired NFL star a perspective that extends far beyond the football field.Kelce became a father while his football career was still developing. He and Kylie Kelce welcomed their first daughter, Wyatt, in 2019, followed by Elliotte in 2021 and Bennett in 2023. Their fourth daughter, Finnley, arrived in March 2025.Raising four children has given Jason and Kylie plenty of chaotic moments. It has also created a family dynamic that the former NFL star clearly treasures.Jason has spoken openly about the difference between trying to teach his children and realizing that they are teaching him, too.“We had zero girls in the household growing up other than Mom [Donna Kelce], so it was a very testosterone-dominated household,” Jason told E! News in September 2023. “But my girls are so young right now. And I only have girls, so I don’t know what it’s like to be a boy dad really.All I know is a girl dad. And I love my girls. I love my children. They teach me things sometimes when I think that I’m trying to teach them.”That admission says plenty about how Kelce views his role as a father. His daughters are not simply growing up around an NFL legend. They are helping shape the person he is becoming after football.He even found himself reflecting on a children's book in a completely different way.“For instance, I’m reading the kids’ book Oh, The Places You’ll Go! [by] Dr. Seuss, and it’s in the documentary. And I’m like, ‘I feel like I’m getting more out of this than the kids are right now.’”The moment is easy to relate to. Parents often expect to be the ones providing wisdom. Kelce's experience suggests the relationship works both ways.Four children can turn an ordinary day into a logistical challenge. Jason and Kylie have learned that teamwork matters.Kylie once explained that they divide responsibilities depending on the children's ages and needs.“Bennie, I’ve been less on because I’ve been handling Wyatt and Elliotte,” Jason said during a September 2023 episode of his podcast. “Here’s the thing: You gotta have strategies [and] there’s techniques involved.”Kylie added that Jason usually takes responsibility for the toddlers while she handles the newborn.That arrangement reflects something many parents eventually discover. There is no perfect formula for raising children. What works one week may fail the next. Parents have to adjust, communicate and sometimes simply survive the chaos.Kylie has also joked about Jason's ability to handle baby duty.“I think my headphones cut out,” Kylie joked. “But then, who’s watching you? … I’d probably leave you for one hour. I feel like Travis can stand longer than you can, [Jason]. That’s a game-changer when it comes to watching small babies: Bennett right now, she’s happy as a clam if you get up and walk around with her. [Jason] isn’t willing to make that commitment. His back locks up and then that’s the end of it.”The humor behind the exchange shows the couple's willingness to laugh at the messy parts of parenting rather than pretend they have everything figured out.Jason's approach to fatherhood is only one part of the family's parenting philosophy. Kylie has also spoken about the example parents set through everyday language.During a 2024 appearance on Good Morning America, she explained why she pays close attention to the way she talks about her own body around her daughters.“I am now hyper aware of how I talk about myself and my body. Not only in front of my daughters, but in front of my players,” Kylie explained during a January 2024 appearance on Good Morning America. “I think it’s important to model that positive body talk about yourself because then they are taking that away from what you’re doing.”She wants her daughters to learn self-respect by seeing it modeled at home.“We’re making it a point right now to emphasize a positive tone when we talk about anything bodywise,” she said. “Like our one daughter will sort of rub her belly and I’m like, ‘Oh, that is the most beautiful belly I’ve ever seen.'”It is a lesson that goes beyond appearance. Children absorb the way adults speak about themselves. For the Kelces, creating a healthy environment means thinking carefully about those small moments.Fame and wealth could easily create a very different childhood for the Kelce daughters. Jason and Kylie, however, have repeatedly emphasized keeping their children grounded.Kylie explained that family and close friends play an important role in maintaining that sense of normalcy.“We stay surrounded by family and friends, so we keep the people around us very close to us,” Kylie told Us. “Then, we make sure that anything that we’re doing that they feel supported by their family and friends and then also not really putting them in any places of privilege.”She also joked about what she hopes their daughters' future cars will look like.“[We’re] trying our best to make sure that when they grow up and they turn 16, they will be driving a [used vehicle]. We can’t let them have a hand-me-down car at this point. You’re not getting Dad’s [Tesla] CyberTruck as your hand-me-down. You will be driving a basic model, hopefully, having to roll the windows down with a crank.”The family has also accepted that parenting cannot always be done alone. Kylie has been open about using childcare, even when Jason is at home.“My husband could tell me 72 times that he is going to be in the house during the time when I have to leave it, [and] I will still schedule childcare,” Kylie explained in December 2024, adding it’s “not a knock” on Jason. “My husband is busier than he has ever been. I see him less now in retirement than I did when he was playing football. We had a set schedule then, now it is an absolute free-for-all.”That honesty may be one of the most relatable parts of their parenting story. Behind the fame, the podcasts and the NFL legacy is a family trying to figure things out one day at a time.Jason Kelce's greatest lesson from fatherhood may therefore be surprisingly simple. Children do not just need parents who teach them how to succeed. They need parents willing to listen, learn and grow alongside them.For a man who spent years being judged by wins, losses and championships, that may be the most valuable scorecard of all.
Article Summary: Jason Kelce and his wife Kylie have four children. The couple divide responsibilities depending on the children's ages and needs. Jason has spoken openly about the difference between trying to teach his children and realizing that they are teaching him, too. Kylie has also talked about the example parents set through everyday language.

Article Title: Mohammed Kaif 'surprised' by BCCI's struggle to hire top medical professionals amid injury crisis
Article Text:
Mohammed Kaif and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia (Images: Agencies)

VVS Laxman reveals BCCI's struggle to hire CoE staff

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mohammad Kaif questions BCCI's inability to attract top medical experts

India's growing injury crisis has raised fresh questions over the functioning of the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE), with former cricketer Mohammad Kaif expressing surprise that the world's richest cricket board has struggled to recruit some of the world's leading medical and rehabilitation professionals.The latest setback came with Sai Sudharsan being ruled out of India's upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka due to a toe injury. He joins Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar on the list of players unavailable for the Sri Lanka series because of injuries.The repeated injury setbacks have frustrated the BCCI, particularly as several players have had to make trips to the CoE in Bengaluru for rehabilitation. The issue also came into focus when BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia travelled to Bengaluru to discuss the situation with CoE head VVS Laxman.Laxman, during a press conference, revealed that the BCCI has been facing difficulties in finding the right personnel for the CoE. According to him, the board had approached several candidates, but some potential appointments fell through at the final stage.The revelation has now drawn a strong reaction from Kaif, who questioned how the BCCI, despite its enormous financial resources, has been unable to bring some of the best medical professionals and physiotherapists into its setup."There was a statement from VVS Laxman that they had approached several people. Those things were being worked out, but at the last minute, they turned it down. So, what I am trying to say is that whatever is happening needs to be fixed. I am not an expert on this. The experts appointed by the BCCI need to do their job. But I am telling you that it is having a significant impact," Kaif said on his YouTube channel.Kaif admitted that he was particularly surprised by the situation given the financial strength of the BCCI and the attractiveness of working with Indian cricket."Now, I am surprised because so many people are eager to work with the BCCI. We have so much money that if we call someone, they will come running. They do, don't they? Just look at the players. Players leave their countries' matches to come and play in the IPL. They come, don't they?" Kaif said.He further questioned why the BCCI had not been able to finalise contracts with leading physiotherapists and medical experts."So, I was a little surprised that we haven't been able to work things out with some of the world's best physiotherapists and medical professionals and get them to work with the BCCI. I am surprised because we pay so much. We offer such good contracts. If someone comes and works here, they are bound to make a lot of money. They get paid very well," he added.The timing of the concerns is significant, with India heading into a two-Test series against Sri Lanka without several key players. The series begins in Galle on August 15.
Article Summary: Mohammad Kaif questions BCCI's inability to attract top medical experts. Sai Sudharsan ruled out of India's upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka due to a toe injury. He joins Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar on list of players unavailable for Sri Lanka series.

Article Title: BWF: World’s best set for Delhi showdown as Lakshya Sen, PV Sindhu face star-studded field
Article Text:
PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen headline India's medal hopes (Images: Agencies)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The return of the BWF World Championships to India after 17 years will see an international field ready to test singles stars Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu . The event, scheduled from Aug 17-23 at the Indira Gandhi indoor stadium, will bring together the sport’s biggest names, with reigning world champions, Olympic gold medallists and former world No. 1s lining up for a battle.In men’s singles, China’s world No. 1 and reigning world champion Shi Yu Qi will start among the favourites, meeting India’s Ayush Shetty in the opener. The 30-year-old, who claimed his maiden world title in 2025 after finishing runner-up in 2018, combines deceptive strokeplay with tactical nous and an ability to control rallies.Thailand’s Kunlavut Vitidsarn, the 2023 world champion and Paris Olympics silver medallist, adds a threat. A three-time world junior champion, Kunlavut has established himself as one of the toughest players on the circuit with his movement, patience and composure under pressure.For India, much will rest on Sen. The 2021 world bronze medallist made history by becoming the first Indian man to reach an Olympic singles semifinal in Paris, finishing fourth. With home support behind him, the 24-year-old will look to turn a major occasion into a medal-winning run.The women’s field is equally imposing. Sindhu, India’s first world champion and a five-time World Championships medallist, enters her home campaign on the back of a historic 2026 Japan Open triumph. The two-time Olympic medallist remains one of India’s biggest medal hopes.Standing in her way is South Korea’s An Se Young, the reigning Olympic and 2023 world champion, who completed a career Grand Slam by winning the Badminton Asia Championships this year.Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi, a three-time world champion, is a contender while China’s Wang Zhi Yi, the 2026 All England champion and former world No. 1, arrives in form. Olympic champion Chen Yufei, runner-up at last year’s Worlds, will also chase the individual title missing from her collection.
Article Summary: The BWF World Championships will return to India after 17 years. The event is scheduled from Aug 17-23 at the Indira Gandhi indoor stadium. Shi Yu Qi, Ayush Shetty and Kunlavut Vitidsarn are among the favourites in men's singles.

Article Title: 'I would be very worried': Former Sri Lankan cricketer names India's biggest weapon
Article Text:
India’s Rishabh Pant and Shubman Gill (PTI Photo)

Maharoof warns Sri Lanka about Rishabh Pant threat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Sri Lanka all-rounder Farveez Maharoof believes India could opt for three spinners in the opening Test against Sri Lanka, with young left-arm spinner Manav Suthar potentially getting the nod ahead of uncapped off-spinner Saransh Jain.India will be without the retired Ravichandran Ashwin and injured Washington Sundar for the first Test, leaving Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav as the likely first-choice spinners. The bigger selection question is who joins them in the XI.Maharoof feels Suthar could have an advantage because of his ability to extract bounce from the surface. Sri Lankan pitches can offer assistance to spinners through bounce rather than simply producing substantial turn, making that quality particularly useful.Suthar made an impressive start to his international career, claiming seven wickets on his debut against Afghanistan. Jain, meanwhile, is yet to make his India debut but has also put himself in contention after touring Sri Lanka with India A.The 31-year-old off-spinner picked up seven wickets on that tour and also contributed an unbeaten 70 while batting at No. 7.However, Maharoof believes Suthar's ability to generate bounce could outweigh the benefit of having an off-spinner for variation, even if that would leave India with three left-arm spinners."If you ask me, I would be tempted to go with the two left-arm spinners as well as Kuldeep Yadav. Kuldeep is a frontrunner to start in Galle, especially considering his record and the number of wickets he took in the last Test against Afghanistan."I see three spinners for India. Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav and either Suthar or Jain. Ideally, you would like an off-spinner for variation, but I would not be surprised if Manav Suthar plays because his ability to get bounce off the surface could be very handy in Galle."Maharoof expects India to go into the Test with a balanced attack comprising three spinners and two seamers."Overall, looking at India's bowling line-up, it is quite competitive, with two seamers and three spinners."Maharoof also singled out Rishabh Pant as a major threat for Sri Lanka, despite the wicketkeeper-batter's modest returns in India's three-day warm-up game in Colombo.Pant scored just two and 28 in the match, which India won by six wickets. However, Maharoof believes those scores should not give Sri Lanka any confidence ahead of the Test, given Pant's ability to transform a match within a short period."If I were in the Sri Lankan dressing room, I would be very worried about Rishabh Pant. He is a player who, within half an hour or 45 minutes, can completely change the game."We have seen him do it in the past. He has that X-factor and has been given the licence to play his natural game. He is going to face a lot of left-arm spin and off-spin.Maharoof expects Sri Lanka to rely heavily on spin against Pant, predicting that the hosts will field two frontline spinners along with two part-time options. But he believes Pant's unconventional approach could still make him difficult to contain."Sri Lanka will surely go with two frontline spinners as well as two part-timers, but the way Pant scores runs, with his unorthodox style, he is going to be dangerous."
Article Summary: Farveez Maharoof believes India could opt for three spinners in the opening Test against Sri Lanka. Young left-arm spinner Manav Suthar could get the nod ahead of uncapped off-spinner Saransh Jain. India will be without the retired Ravichandran Ashwin and injured Washington Sundar for the first Test.

Article Title: 'They play too many T20s and ODIs': Kapil Dev blames white-ball schedule for India's struggles against spin
Article Text:
Veteran cricketer Kapil Dev (ANI Photo/Sumit)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: It has been more than a year-and-a-half but India’s crushing 0-3 Test series defeat to New Zealand at home still rankles. The Indian batters’ repeated struggle against spin was particularly alarming. The concerns only deepened when the team followed it up with a 0-2 series loss to South Africa, again at home.Now, as India gear up for a two-Test series against Sri Lanka, their ability to negotiate spin will once again come under the scanner. The first Test begins in Galle on Saturday with the conditions expected to be spin-friendly. Former India captain Kapil Dev believes the problem goes beyond technique. He feels the players’ heavy white-ball cricket schedule has affected their preparedness and performance in the longest format.“India recently have not been at th-eir best against spin bowling because they play too many T20s and One-Da-yers. Test cricket is a different ball ga-me but I hope they can put their head together and play better in Sri Lanka,” said the 1983 World Cup-winning captain, who was in the city to launch the Bengaluru Blasters team, ahead of the inaugural JITO Premier League.Kapil also advocated the importance of international players playing domestic cricket. “Playing domestic cricket is very important. The reason why Indian teams struggle against spin is that the top players don’t play enough domestic cricket. That’s where the BCCI should put its foot down and make everyone play three-day and four-day matches.The other aspect is that the younger generation will get to learn from top players in domestic cricket,” Kapil said.One of the highlights of Kapil’s 121-Test career, which spanned 16 years, was that he never missed a Test due to injury. Given the change in the workload of players, Kapil, who said it was unfair to compare eras, joked about the secret to remaining injury-free: “My mom is no more; otherwise, she could have given a few recipes.”On a serious note, the pace legend emphasised the importance of understanding the body and preparations. “One should know about one’s own body. There is too much T20 and ODI cricket happening, so you have to be careful about the toll it takes on the body. Our body is actually not tuned to being a fast bowler. Our body is more tuned to being a batsman. The BCCI should look into how much workload to give fast bowlers,” said the 67-year-old.
Article Summary: Former India captain Kapil Dev believes the problem goes beyond technique. He feels the players’ heavy white-ball cricket schedule has affected their preparedness and performance in the longest format. The first Test begins in Galle on Saturday with the conditions expected to be spin-friendly.

Article Title: Duan Jansen, Marco’s twin brother, earns maiden South Africa call-up for Namibia tour
Article Text:
Duan Jansen (Photo by Getty Images)

Duan Jansen gets his chance

South Africa look to build depth

Duan Jansen, twin brother of South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen , has earned his maiden senior call-up and could make his international debut during South Africa’s upcoming white-ball tour of Namibia.The 15-member squad, led by experienced spinner Bjorn Fortuin , will play a T20I tri-series involving Namibia and Zimbabwe before taking on Namibia in a historic three-match ODI series.The T20I tri-series will be played in Windhoek from August 28 to September 6, followed by three ODIs against Namibia from September 9 to 13. The ODI series will be the first bilateral 50-over contest between the two neighbouring countries.Duan’s selection comes after an impressive 2025/26 domestic season. He was named Division 1 One Day Cup Player of the Year and played a key role in helping the Titans win the title, scoring an unbeaten 61 in the final against the Lions.Eathan Bosch is the other uncapped T20I player, while Connor Esterhuizen, Jordan Hermann and Nqobani Mokoena have received their first ODI call-ups.“We’ve selected one squad for both series as we feel we have all departments well covered and it provides a great opportunity for players to build on their international caps.We saw glimpses of what Connor and Nqobani can offer during the T20I series against New Zealand earlier this year. It was unfortunate that Jordan picked up an injury in the opening match of that series, so we’re looking forward to seeing him get another opportunity at this level.Coach Shukri Conrad said using the same squad for both formats would give the players greater continuity and valuable international exposure. Nationally contracted players Dewald Brevis, Tony de Zorzi and Kwena Maphaka will provide additional experience.“This tour has also opened the door for players who have performed domestically. Duan is one of those players. He is a quality all-rounder who has also shown great character for the Titans. Bjorn is an experienced player and proven leader who has successfully captained the Lions, and we have every confidence in his ability to lead this group. It is always exciting to play against our neighbouring countries, and the first-ever ODI series between South Africa and Namibia adds further significance, especially as we build towards next year’s World Cup,” he added.South Africa are scheduled to leave Johannesburg for Windhoek on August 25.
Article Summary: Duan Jansen could make his international debut during South Africa’s upcoming white-ball tour of Namibia. The 15-member squad, led by experienced spinner Bjorn Fortuin, will play a T20I tri-series involving Namibia and Zimbabwe before taking on Namibia in a historic three-match ODI series.

Article Title: Born in Cristiano Ronaldo's hometown, former Australia cricketer to lead Portugal's T20 World Cup bid
Article Text:
Moises Henriques of Australia (second from left), and Cristiano Ronaldo

Portugal fixtures:

Former Australia all-rounder Moises Henriques will captain Portugal as they attempt to qualify for the T20 World Cup for the first time.Henriques, who played four Tests, 16 ODIs and 24 T20Is for Australia, will lead Portugal's 14-member squad at the T20 World Cup Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C in Finland.The Portuguese Cricket Federation announced the squad on Tuesday, with Henriques named captain. He was born in Madeira, the hometown of Portugal football captain Cristiano Ronaldo , before his family moved to Australia when he was a child.Henriques played 24 T20Is, 16 ODIs and four Tests for Australia. His last international appearance came in August 2021, when he played a T20I against Bangladesh. He became eligible to represent Portugal in June after completing the required three-year cooling-off period for players switching from an ICC Full Member to an Associate nation.Henriques announced last month that he was retiring from Australian domestic cricket but would continue playing overseas. He has a contract with Glasgow Cosmic for the inaugural season of the European T20 Premier League. On Monday, he was also named Portugal's captain for their T20 World Cup qualifying campaign in Finland.Portugal are ranked 37th in the ICC men's T20I rankings. They will face Israel, Germany, Greece and Czechia in Group B of the T20 World Cup Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C from August 14 to 20.The group winner will face the winner of Group A in the final on August 21.The winner of the qualifier will advance to the European regional final, where Scotland, Jersey and Denmark will join them. The top two teams from the regional final will then qualify for the global qualifier as they bid to reach the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand.Portugal's squad also features Craig Cachopa, the former Sussex, Auckland and Wellington wicketkeeper-batter; Cameron Shekleton, who has represented South Africa A; Sebastian de Oliveira, who played one List A match for Gauteng alongside Ryan Rickelton; and Bangladesh-born spinner Siraj Ullah Khadem, who was included in the longlist for this year's Hundred auction.Henriques takes over the captaincy from Carlos Nunes, who captains Twickenham in the Middlesex County Cricket League in England. Nunes remains part of the 14-member squad.Moises Henriques (capt), Craig Cachopa, Edward Fleming, Christopher de Freitas, Rahulkumar Hashu, Siraj Ullah Khadem, Hardeep Khuttan, Jeremy Martins, Dhavalkumar Norotam (wk), Jordan Netto, Carlos Nunes, Sebastian de Oliveira, Upen Shantu, Cameron Shekleton.vs Israel (August 14), vs Germany (August 15), vs Greece (August 17), vs Czechia (August 20), Final (August 21).

Portugal will face Israel, Germany, Greece and Czechia in Group B of the T20 World Cup Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C.

Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry , have always been united no matter what they have faced in their life and marriage. Their love has inspired millions but the two have often been criticised for their relationship. Ahead of the new season, Ayesha Curry has shared an update about what the family is up to.A few hours ago, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry took to her social media to share a wholesome post about their family.One of the pictures posted by her shows their two boys playing together while another shows Stephen Curry cuddling with his son on a private jet.The caption of the post reads as, “These are my boys” and fans are here for it.Over the last few years, amid the widespread criticism, Stephen Curry has grown increasingly private about his life and prefers to stay out of the spotlight during the offseason.As the Golden State Warriors’ star player Stephen Curry gears up for the new season, Ayesha Curry is also gearing up for the release of her new romantic comedy Second Chance Holiday, all set to premiere on Roku this holiday seasonWith this being the first time Ayesha Curry will be acting as a lead, she opened up about it in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter.Stephen Curry's wife Ayesha Curry said, “Gosh, honestly, it’s such a big moment for me, personally. It’s a rom-com, so of course it’s silly and playful. That’s fine. But for me, it was my first No. 1 on the call sheet for a movie.”The “Sweet July” founder added, “Stephen was like, “You go and do it. I got this.” I actually got to see a bunch of footage yesterday, and it made me think, “Wow, I did it.” It’s my ultimate dream. Article Title: ‘Shock and disbelief’: Arkansas football player discovers ‘venomous snake’ hiding inside his helmet during practice
Article Text:
‘Shock and disbelief’: Arkansas football player discovers ‘venomous snake’ hiding inside his helmet during practice

Kirk Horton reacts after Maumelle High School football player finds snake

Chris Davis explains why the Maumelle High School snake discovery was so unusual

A high school football player in Arkansas unknowingly practiced for nearly an hour with a venomous snake inside his helmet before he felt something moving. Coaches at Maumelle High School discovered the roughly two-foot-long snake tucked under the helmet padding after the player raised the alarm during practice on August 6. Animal Services later identified it as a cottonmouth, removed it safely and released it in a wooded area away from the school. The player was not bitten and was given another helmet so he could return to practice. The incident has now led the team to remind players to check their equipment before wearing it.The player noticed unusual movement inside his helmet and took the problem to his defensive coach. The coach then alerted athletic director Kirk Horton, who helped deal with the situation. The snake was difficult to reach because it had slipped underneath the helmet’s padding.Speaking to KARK, Horton said, ‘It really was just shock and disbelief,’ and added, ‘I’ve got a better shot at winning the lottery than seeing this in my ten years.’Staff placed the helmet inside a tote bag while they waited for Maumelle Animal Services. Director Chris Davis said, ‘When the officers got there and stuff, they examined the helmet, and at that time they could see that there was a snake in the helmet,’ before officials confirmed it was not a copperhead and believed it was a cottonmouth or water snake.The animal was later confirmed as a cottonmouth. It was removed from the helmet and taken to a forested area away from the school. The player received a new helmet and continued practicing.Davis said the incident was unlike anything he had dealt with during his work with animals. Speaking to KATV, he said, ‘I’ve removed a snake out of a car vent, in the engine, purses, backpacks,’ he said. ’In a helmet? Never.‘It was very unreal. You had to kind of be there and take pictures to say this was real.’The snake had been hiding in a dark, protected part of the helmet, keeping it out of sight while the player practiced. Davis said the player was fortunate not to be bitten. He also warned about the danger of the species, saying, ‘The cottonmouth, in my opinion, is probably the second most venomous snake here in Arkansas. I would say the rattlesnake is probably the number one.’Animal Services had to wash the helmet out so the snake could be safely removed. It was then relocated away from the school rather than killed.The team later held a safety meeting and told players to check their equipment before putting it on. That advice came after the snake had remained hidden inside the helmet for almost an hour.For the player, a normal football practice turned into a frightening discovery. He had worn the helmet for close to an hour before noticing movement. Fortunately, the snake was found before anyone was bitten.
Article Summary: Arkansas football player discovers'venomous snake' hiding inside his helmet during practice. Coaches at Maumelle High School discovered the roughly two- foot-long snake tucked under the helmet padding after the player raised the alarm during practice on August 6. Animal Services later identified it as a cottonmouth, removed it safely and released it in a wooded area away from the school.

Article Title: Zach Holland’s ‘shocking’ golf cheating scandal: How a fake hole-in-one exposed his secret before tournament glory

How Zach Holland’s fake hole-in-one was exposed

Zach Holland has resigned from WingHaven Country Club in Missouri after admitting he faked a hole-in-one during a tournament. The college golfer placed a ball in the cup before play, then told his group he had hit the ace. Security footage later showed him near the fourth green before his tee time, exposing the trick. Holland later admitted what he had done during an interview with 101 ESPN St. Louis, saying, “There’s no excuse for what I did, and I was completely in the wrong.” The incident has brought questions about his standing among golfers.The incident happened at the par-3 fourth hole during a WingHaven tournament with a hole-in-one prize pot. On the morning of the event, Holland told his playing partners that his grandmother had fallen and was being taken to hospital. He said he might need to take a call and would move ahead.Holland later returned and said he had “thinned” his tee shot and could not see where it landed. His partners found a Titleist in the cup and believed he had made an ace. At 8.20am, Holland posted in a group chat: “Holy s***. He shoots, he scores.”The story changed when players noticed that nobody had clearly seen the ball go into the cup. One golfer also questioned the pitch mark shown in Holland’s video. Club staff were contacted, and cameras near the fourth hole were checked.According to the Daily Mail, the footage showed Holland arriving near the fourth green at about 6.20am, well before his tee time. He got out of his vehicle, walked towards the green, disappeared from view and returned about two minutes later. The cameras did not show him placing the ball in the cup.Holland initially denied wrongdoing. After officials told him about the footage, he resigned his WingHaven membership and his team’s tournament result was removed from the standings.Holland later spoke about the incident on 101 ESPN St. Louis. He said he had made a mistake and accepted the consequences.“You do something as dumb as I did, there are consequences for that,” Holland said. “There’s no excuse for what I did, and I was completely in the wrong.”He also said his family had faced online abuse. “What I am most worried about is my family. … It’s not fair to them for me to put them in that situation where when they walk through a room, there is a stigma there that your dad is a [cheater].”Holland, 34, played college golf at William Carey University. The St. Louis District Golf Association has also listed him as a WingHaven player and recorded tournament success with Adam Tomicich in 2025.WingHaven general manager Nathan Charnes said the club had acted quickly. “We care deeply about the integrity of the game and the experience we provide for our members and guests. Because this situation involved the actions of an individual and has been resolved, we consider it closed and have no further comment.”
Article Summary: College golfer Zach Holland faked a hole-in-one during a tournament. He placed a ball in the cup before play, then told his group he had hit the ace. Security footage later showed him near the fourth green before his tee time, exposing the trick. Holland later admitted what he had done during an interview with 101 ESPN St. Louis.

Article Title: HasanAbi calls for permanent Asmongold ban from Twitch and YouTube as streamer feud explodes

Why I'm Gone

HasanAbi has reignited a fierce debate over streamer moderation after arguing that Asmongold should face permanent bans from both Twitch and YouTube . His comments came after Asmongold defended remarks that led to his recent Twitch suspension. Hasan questioned whether major platforms still enforce their rules consistently, while also pointing to what he sees as growing pressure from political groups and online campaigns.During a livestream on August 9, HasanAbi responded to Asmongold’s YouTube video, in which the streamer addressed his two-week Twitch suspension. The controversy followed comments in which Asmongold described immigrants using dehumanizing language and advocated shooting people, including children, in a discussion about immigration.Rather than apologizing, Asmongold said he stood by his comments. That response became the focus of Hasan’s criticism.Hasan argued that Asmongold appeared to be testing how far Twitch and YouTube would allow him to go before taking stronger action. He also compared the current moderation environment with what he believes would have happened several years ago."It's pretty wild that I feel like this is a test. Right? He's basically testing the boundaries of Twitch to be like, 'Listen, what are you going to do? I'm not apologetic.I don't care. I said what I said. Go ahead, keep me banned if you can. What's wild about it is I feel like this is also testing the boundaries of YouTube's terms of service, too. Because I feel like YouTube back in the day would quite literally ban someone for statements like this one. "The argument places Asmongold’s suspension within a much larger discussion about platform rules. Twitch and YouTube have enormous creator communities, and decisions involving controversial political speech can quickly become flashpoints.Hasan also took aim at the business pressures he believes influence moderation decisions. He suggested that platforms may be increasingly cautious about taking action against prominent creators whose audiences could respond aggressively."Oh, my god! It does say a lot about how things have gotten as far as like corporate culture in general that this will probably be a slap on the wrist by Twitch because they are ******* terrified of angering the right-wing masses that have spent a good deal of time doxxing people that work for the trust and safety team at Twitch. It's like really ****** up!"Hasan went even further, saying Asmongold would likely have faced a permanent ban under the standards he remembers from previous years. He brought up Destiny as another example of a creator who, in his view, received harsher punishment for less serious remarks."This would be an insta perma. Like, there is no shot! I would say, pre-Trump 2.0, this is a perma. Like, Destiny got banned for less, which is crazy to say. Like, he got perma'd for less, and he definitely deserved it! So, I don't even know where we're at now. You know? I feel like this would be a ban on ******* YouTube as well! Or at least a demonetization on YouTube as well!"The dispute now raises a familiar question for Twitch and YouTube: where should platforms draw the line between controversial political commentary and speech that violates their rules?Asmongold had not publicly responded to HasanAbi’s latest comments at the time of the report. For now, the clash between the two creators highlights how moderation decisions can become political battles of their own, particularly when major streamers are involved.

Article Title: “I almost started crying afterward”: 54-year-old surfer Kelly Slater gets emotional after near-perfect showdown in Monster Tahiti wave

Kelly Slater’s near-perfect performance at the Tahiti Pro left the 54-year-old surfing legend fighting back tears after he defeated three-time world champion Gabriel Medina at Teahupo’o on Aug. 10. Slater posted a 19.06 heat score out of 20, using two deep barrels to produce scores of 9.73 and 9.33.The result is quite emotional for Slater, who stepped away from full-time competition in 2024 and has been recovering from hip surgery. Given a wildcard for the event, he now has another chance to compete on one of surfing’s most demanding stages.Kelly Slater knew the matchup with Medina would test more than his surfing. Medina had won the Tahiti Pro twice and had previously beaten Slater in the 2014 final. The Brazilian also arrived with his own difficult stretch behind him, something Slater understood from experience.“Everyone knows Gabe’s been through a lot lately,” Slater said after the heat. “It’s tough to come all this way and lose to someone who’s not in the title race. I’m on the other side of that now, so I feel all those emotions, the toughness of the travel, being away from family.”The emotion caught Slater by surprise. “When you have a loss, it sucks. That was a very emotional heat,” he shared. “I almost started crying afterward.”For a surfer who has spent decades handling pressure at the highest level, the moment showed how much the competition still means to him. Slater said he had to control his nerves before committing to the heavier sections of Teahupo’o.“I definitely had to settle in. I knew going against [Medina], he’s just so savvy as a competitor,” he said. “I tried to push a bit deeper. I started doing breathing exercises, calming down and getting the heart rate down.”Teahupo’o is hardly a forgiving place for a veteran returning from surgery. The wave, which hosted Olympic surfing during the 2024 Paris Games, is renowned for its power and precision.Slater had already won the Tahiti Pro five times between 2000 and 2016, but his latest appearance came with questions about whether the wildcard should have gone to a local surfer.“Obviously, you see the comments, a lot of people doubting me or saying they should’ve given the wildcard to a local, and I get why people say that,” Slater said. “Without pressure, you’ve got no diamonds. It fired me up, and even after all this time, yeah, I have something to prove.”His response was unmistakable in the water. His 19.06 total fell just short of the perfect 20 he had produced twice at Teahupo’o, while also reminding everyone why he is an 11-time world champion.Slater will next face Australia’s Jack Robinson in the third round.Away from competition, Slater has also entered another chapter of his life with longtime girlfriend Kalani Miller. The couple recently shared news of their growing family, including their daughter Azumi Moon and son Tao.That personal backdrop added another layer to Slater’s comments about travel, competition and being away from home. After the Medina heat, he described the experience as a “great life memory.”“Super emotional heat for me and for Gabe, I had a good time,” Slater said.Now comes another demanding test against Robinson. The question is no longer whether Slater can still produce one extraordinary wave. He has already answered that at Teahupo’o. The next question is how far this latest run can carry him.

Article Title: Buffalo Bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1B stadium
Article Text:
Buffalo Bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1B stadium(Getty)

Buffalo Bills explain their position as viral seat photos create early controversy around new Highmark Stadium

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Buffalo Bills expected fans to leave the new Highmark Stadium talking about the atmosphere. Instead, many left talking about blocked views.Photos from Saturday’s Blue and Red practice spread rapidly across social media. Fans showed railings, stair structures and overhangs cutting into their sightlines. Within hours, the excitement around the $2.2 billion stadium turned into a heated debate among Bills fans.More than 51,000 fans attended the first public event at the new stadium, and many praised the steep seating bowl and the energy inside the building. However, the viral photos quickly changed the conversation.Several personal seat license holders compared the actual view from their seats with the virtual renderings they saw before buying. Some felt the real experience did not match what they expected after spending thousands of dollars on seat licenses.The Bills responded by acknowledging the feedback and promising further review. A team spokesperson told Sportico that Saturday’s practice served as an important test for the new facility.“Saturday’s practice was a great opportunity to test the new stadium,” the spokesperson said. “We are currently addressing internal and external feedback regarding the facility’s operation following the first event.We’ll uutilisethe next six weeks to refine any details as we prepare for the home opener on Thursday, Sept. 17.”That statement became the clearest indication that the organisation plans to make adjustments before the regular-season debut against the Detroit Lions.The controversy grew because some of the images reached millions of people online. One Associated Press photo from a seat not used for Bills games drew millions of views on X, while a compilation of obstructed-view photos spread even further. Some fans claimed the railings affected the first several rows across many upper-deck sections.At the same time, other supporters pushed back and shared positive experiences from their visit. According to reports, the team has heard from fewer than 1% of personal seat license holders regarding sightline concerns.The new stadium represents a major project for Buffalo. The Bills, Erie County and New York State agreed to the stadium deal in 2022, with $850 million in public funding helping keep the franchise in Western New York. The previous stadium opened in 1973.Architectural firm Populous designed the venue with a steep seating bowl intended to bring the upper deck closer to the field. Open concourses were also designed to maintain views of the action from many areas of the building.The team chose a canopy structure instead of a full dome. The canopy aims to protect roughly two-thirds of the seats from weather while also helping trap crowd noise inside the stadium.The Bills exceeded expectations in seat-license sales, generating about $260 million from more than 53,000 PSLs. Virtual seat views played a significant role in that sales process, which is why the comparison between renderings and real-world views became such a sensitive issue.Ticketmaster identifies some locations as obstructed-view seats, but several buyers believe the warning did not fully reflect the actual experience.Most early reviews of the new Highmark Stadium remain positive. Still, the viral seat photos created an early public-relations challenge. Bills fans now want more than explanations. They want proof that the vast majority of seats deliver the clear view promised during the long wait for the team’s new home.

Article Title: Why was Matt Miller hit with a misdemeanor charge? 42-year-old ESPN analyst’s incident explained
Article Text:

Matt Miller hit with misdemeanor charge

What Miller has said publicly

A second, separate investigation looms

ESPN NFL draft analyst Matt Miller has been formally charged over the June car crash that nearly killed him and cost him his left arm. Jasper County, Missouri prosecutors filed a Class A misdemeanor count against the 42-year-old for failing to drive on the right half of the roadway, the same failure that sent his Ford Bronco into an oncoming semi-truck on June 17.Miller is due in Jasper County Circuit Court on September 21. If convicted, he faces up to a year in jail and a fine. The truck driver was not hurt.Court filings reviewed Monday show the charge stems directly from dash-cam footage of the crash, later released by TMZ. The video captured Miller's SUV drifting across the center line on the state highway before colliding head-on with the 18-wheeler. He was ejected from the vehicle on impact.The injuries were severe enough that doctors had to choose between saving Miller's leg and saving his arm. They saved the leg. His left arm did not survive.Miller has largely stayed off the record since the crash, but he posted an update on X in July confirming the outcome of his surgeries. "The surgery to remove my left arm was successful," he wrote, adding that his medical team had managed to save his leg. He said he was stepping away from ESPN indefinitely to focus on recovery.“Similarly, the femur and patella surgeries were also successful and the fantastic surgery team was able to save my left leg. To best focus on my healing and recovery, I’m stepping away indefinitely and will be placed on leave from ESPN. Thank you to all for the prayers and thoughts; please keep them coming.”The misdemeanor charge isn't Miller's only legal exposure. Following the crash, Awful Announcing reported dozens of allegations spanning Miller's career involving unpaid winnings from charity fantasy football leagues, along with claims he took payment for draft scouting lessons he never delivered. Those allegations prompted the Missouri Attorney General's office to open a financial impropriety investigation, which remains active and is separate from the Jasper County traffic charge. ESPN has not yet commented on either matter.For now, Miller's next fixed date is the September 21 arraignment. Whether ESPN addresses his status before then, or waits on the AG's findings, is still an open question. Further updates await.
Article Summary: NFL draft analyst Matt Miller has been formally charged over the June car crash that nearly killed him and cost him his left arm. Jasper County, Missouri prosecutors filed a Class A misdemeanor count against the 42-year-old for failing to drive on the right half of the roadway. Miller is due in Jasper County Circuit Court on September 21. If convicted, he faces up to a year in jail and a fine.

Article Title: “Go to hell”: Stephanie White breaks silence with fiery response to not backing Sophie Cunningham
Article Text:
Stephanie White . Image via: Trevor Ruszkowski/ IMAGN Images

Stephanie White reacts to not backing Sophie Cunningham

Indiana Fever president Kelly Krauskopf responds to the fire Stephanie White call

White refuses to apologize for her Carrington comments

Stephanie White has finally addressed the backlash surrounding her handling of the controversial foul on Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, delivering a forceful defense of her players and rejecting claims that she failed to support Cunningham.The controversy followed Indiana’s 90-86 win over the Chicago Sky, when DiJonai Carrington was ejected for a Flagrant 2 after striking Cunningham across the face and neck. White’s decision to defend Carrington’s intentions after the game triggered criticism from some Fever fans. On Tuesday, White made it clear she had no intention of backing away from her position.White said the criticism had become less about the actual play and more about an online narrative questioning her commitment to Indiana’s players.“This isn't necessarily for those people that are in this room,” White began. “This is more for an online community that's trying to create narratives that simply don't exist. Trying to create a fabrication or distortion of who I am, of what I'm about. Our players' success, our players' health and wellness, our players' safety is always a top priority for me.”White explained that she did not see the foul happen in real time because she went directly to her postgame press conference.Once she watched the replay, however, she acknowledged the seriousness of the contact.“Was it egregious?” White went on. “Absolutely. When you have a chance to watch that over and over and over on replay, you can see that. I didn't have that in real time. I take personally, any suggestions that I don't 100% always have my players' back. I ride with them 10 toes down all the time. All the time. They know that.”Her frustration grew as she addressed the wider attention surrounding the Fever.“The reality is with me, I will always lead with love. I will always lead with grace. I will always lead with humility, and I will always lead with integrity,” White said. “That doesn't mean I'll always get it right. I'm also human. The hate, the fear-mongering, the divisiveness, the stuff that's trying to hijack our league will not win.”While White faced criticism online, Fever leadership quickly made its position clear.President Kelly Krauskopf released a statement supporting White and dismissed any suggestion that the organization was considering a coaching change.“Coach White has done a tremendous job leading the Fever and for the second-consecutive season, has us in great position for a playoff push,” Krauskopf said. “She has kept our team focused and united, all while under the brightest spotlight our team and our league have ever experienced. She has the full support of leadership.”That statement matters because Indiana remains firmly in the playoff race. White owns a 44-32 record since taking over the Fever, and Indiana reached the semifinal round during her first season.The Fever also recovered from a 4-4 start this season and moved to 16-8 over their next 24 games. Their offense has been a major reason for the turnaround, with Indiana leading the WNBA in scoring at 95.9 points per game.The original controversy centered on White’s postgame assessment of Carrington, whom she previously coached with the Connecticut Sun.“It was a hard foul,” White said. “I don’t think that DiJonai intentionally came out to get her across the neck like she did. But it did happen, and I thought it was the right call.”White also praised Carrington’s competitive approach, saying she did not believe the guard deliberately targeted Cunningham.That distinction has remained at the heart of the dispute. Cunningham believed the contact was intentional, while White has maintained that the Flagrant 2 call was correct without assigning malicious intent to Carrington.White’s latest remarks did not offer the apology some critics wanted. Instead, she doubled down on her commitment to the Fever locker room.“It won't win,” she said. “We are united, we are connected. We will not be divided. Every day these women put their ass on the line. Every day. When they go low, we go high. Love will win. Grace will win, humility will win and kindness will win. I stand by them, I will always stand by them. Everybody else can go to Hell.”For now, Krauskopf’s message has settled the biggest question surrounding White: her job is not in jeopardy. The Fever’s attention can return to the playoff race, but the debate over White’s handling of Cunningham is unlikely to disappear overnight.
Article Summary: Stephanie White has defended her decision to not back DiJonai Carrington after she was ejected for a Flagrant 2 foul on Sophie Cunningham. White said the criticism had become less about the actual play and more about an online narrative questioning her commitment to her players.

Brock Lesnar and Bill Goldberg are two of the most recognisable heavyweight stars in the history of professional wrestling, and they have taken different career paths, but both have turned championship success and outsized personalities into financial fortunes. Whereas Lesnar became a WWE and UFC champion, Goldberg had an impressive run in WCW and made lucrative returns to WWE and international appearances.Celebrity net-worth numbers are not independently audited and can vary widely from source to source, so these numbers should be taken as estimates and not verified financials. Lesnar’s career has included WWE, UFC, professional football attempts, endorsements and merchandise, giving him multiple major earning phases across combat sports.Goldberg’s money story is more related to pro wrestling, TV, acting, licensing and premium appearances.He used his success in WCW as a base, and followed it up with appearances in WWE, especially on big international shows, allowing him to charge premium rates while working on a more sporadic basis.A wrestler can still make a tonne of money without working a full-time schedule, as Goldberg’s reported financial picture demonstrates. More recent reporting has pegged his WWE base salary at around $5 million, with bonuses, merchandise and event-related revenue potentially pushing total annual compensation considerably higher during active runs.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Brock Lesnar's net worth is expected to be around $25 million in 2026, and Bill Goldberg's will be around $16 million.Brock Lesnar’s total earnings are unique because pro wrestling was just a slice of his financial pie. After winning an NCAA Division I wrestling championship, Lesnar joined WWE and became an instant draw. His first run with WWE made him a marketable heavyweight before he left pro wrestling and went on to other avenues.Recent 2026 reporting also indicates that Lesnar’s latest WWE chapter is now finished. After his SummerSlam bout against Oba Femi, he announced his retirement from professional wrestling, ending a career that saw him win multiple WWE titles and the UFC Heavyweight Championship.Lesnar’s overall financial model has been built on high-value contracts plus multiple elite sporting careers, while Goldberg’s has been more on premium wrestling appearances, licensing and entertainment work.Bill Goldberg took a different path to financial success. He broke out in WCW, where his undefeated streak and dominant presentation made him one of wrestling’s biggest attractions in the late 1990s. At one point, his WCW pay was said to be around $2.5 million per year.One of the biggest parts of Goldberg’s modern earning profile has been his ability to score high-value special appearances. He reportedly was paid around $2 million for each Saudi Arabia match he had during his WWE returns. Then there’s the WWE Legends deal and merchandise revenue that have also provided an additional stream outside of individual bouts.This distinction is important when comparing their total wealth. Instead, their most valuable commercial asset has been their recognisable wrestling characters.The contrast between their lifestyles is striking. Lesnar has been more private and lived in rural areas while Goldberg has been more public with his cars, ranch and entertainment interests. Neither has been dependent on celebrity appearances for financial relevance.Ultimately, the comparison reveals two distinct paths to financial success in the sphere of professional wrestling. Lesnar developed a more extensive athletic resume and leveraged championship success in WWE and UFC into extremely lucrative contracts. Goldberg turned a brief but spectacular WCW high into an entertainment brand that has lasted decades. Both are financially successful examples of wrestlers who turned larger-than-life personas into long-term commercial value.

Article Title: Malaysia's Princess Ilyana, 29, married British GT racer Chris Froggatt, 32; the multi-day Kuala Lumpur wedding blended royal traditions with motorsport
Article Text:

The racer husband

Tengku Puteri Raja Tengku Puteri Ilyana Alia, daughter of the Sultan of Pahang, married British racing driver Christopher Lionel Froggatt in Kuala Lumpur on Friday, August 7.Princess Ilyana, 29, is the daughter of Sultan Abdullah, the Sultan of Pahang who served as Malaysia’s king from 2019 to 2024. Her mother is Julia Rais, a former actress. The bride married Froggatt, 32, who competes as a racing driver in the GT World Challenge Europe Endurance Cup, Town and Country reported.The marriage ceremony was held in Kuala Lumpur, with Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah attending the solemnisation. According to The Star, other members of the Pahang royal family were also present, including Regent of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah and his younger siblings.The ceremony followed Islamic wedding traditions. According to the Kesultanan Pahang’s official Facebook page, Froggatt performed the sunnah prayer before the ceremony continued with the couple’s procession to the dais.The ceremony included the presentation of the ‘mas kahwin’ and the exchange of wedding rings. Prayers were then recited before the couple took part in the ‘merenjis’, a symbolic gesture associated with blessings and prayers for their well-being.The Kesultanan Pahang said the ceremony was attended by members of the Pahang Royal Household. Among those present were Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah, the Crown Prince of Pahang, and other members of the royal family.Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, the Chief Minister of Pahang, was also listed among the guests. Sheik Mohammed bin Hamad bin Tahnoon Al Nahyan of the United Arab Emirates was also present.The wedding took place at the Shangri-La hotel in Kuala Lumpur, according to Town & Country. Images from the ceremony showed the bride and groom seated together in traditional attire during the proceedings.For the wedding, Princess Ilyana wore Queen Azizah’s Diamond Tiara, described as a dramatic heirloom piece. She paired the tiara with a gown by Malaysian designer Radzuan Radziwill.The bride’s royal family background is closely linked to Pahang and Malaysia’s rotating monarchy. Her father, Sultan Abdullah, is the sixth Sultan of Pahang and was the 16th King of Malaysia.Malaysia’s throne is different from a monarchy in which the same royal family remains on the national throne permanently. The country has nine hereditary royal families, and the Conference of Rulers elects one of the nine state rulers to serve as the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, or King of Malaysia, for a five-year term.The bride's father Sultan Abdullah is also the ruler of Pahang, one of the nine states whose hereditary rulers take part in the country’s royal system.Princess Ilyana’s husband, Christopher Lionel Froggatt, has a career in international motor racing. The 32-year-old British driver competes in the GT World Challenge Europe Endurance Cup.His official biography on Tempesta Racing describes his interest in cars as beginning during childhood. He also developed an interest in riding quad bikes and motocross while growing up.According to his racing biography, he arrived in the sport at the age of 24. A Ferrari high-performance driving event at the company’s test track in Fiorano, Italy, later became an important turning point in his move towards international motor racing.His official biography states, “A childhood love of cars, riding quad bikes and motocross from a young age all fuelled his fascination with speed, and his unfashionably late arrival on the car racing scene at 24 years of age.”It adds that an exploratory Ferrari high-performance driving event at Fiorano, which he attended as a guest of a close friend, “proved to be the turning point for Chris and his journey to the starting grid of international motor racing.”Froggatt, who drives a Ferrari 296 GT3, has competed in Ferrari Challenge and GT3 racing. His listed achievements include winning the GT World Challenge Europe Endurance Bronze Cup in 2021 and 2023, and the GT World Challenge Europe Sprint Cup Pro-Am title in 2020.
Article Summary: Princess Ilyana, 29, is the daughter of Sultan Abdullah, the Sultan of Pahang. Her mother is Julia Rais, a former actress. The bride married Froggatt, 32, who competes as a racing driver in the GT World Challenge Europe Endurance Cup.
